messages:
alex_h: Hey - scripting a CI job that switches redwood CLI profiles. Two quick Qs: 1) precedence order for credentials (env var vs profile file vs OS keychain)? 2) when using streaming (--stream) + retries, does the CLI/runtime resume a partial stream or fully restart the request? saw a 401 mid-stream in CI.
maria_s: Short answer: env var wins. Precedence is REDWOOD_API_KEY (or REDWOOD_PROFILE env) > local profile file (~/.redwood/credentials) > OS keychain fallbacks. Avoid committing profile files.
samir: For streaming: retries are at the request level so a retry will restart the stream from the beginning. There is no automatic resume for partial streamed responses today. If you need idempotency, include a client-side token and dedupe on your app side.
olivia: CI tip: use your cloud secret store to inject REDWOOD_API_KEY into the job env. That sidesteps profile file switching entirely. In our pipelines we set REDWOOD_MAX_RETRIES=2 and REDWOOD_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS=500 for moderate retry behavior.
maria_s: Example env-based script we use:```
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$REDBOX_REDLAB_KEY"    # injected by runner
export REDWOOD_PROFILE=staging                 # optional if using profiles
redwood completions --model gpt-redwood-1 --stream --prompt "..."
```Also our local profile file format (if you must):```
[profiles]
staging.api_key = "sk_..."
production.api_key = "sk_..."
```Store that file in ~/.redwood/credentials and never in git.
ci-bot: ci-bot: pipeline #5421 failed: unauthorized (401) while executing step "generate-notes" at 1772010000. See job logs: https://ci.example/5421
samir: The 401 during stream usually means the token rotated/expired mid-request. In CI that's typically short-lived tokens or wrong secret mounting. Also check clock skew on the runner if you're using signed tokens.
alex_h: Awesome — thanks. Plan: switch to secret-injected REDWOOD_API_KEY, set RETRIES=2, and change the job to re-request the last prompt chunk on retry (we'll dedupe using request-id). Will ping once I push. :thumbsup:
maria_s: Nice. If you want, I can share a tiny wrapper we use to checkpoint streaming chunks (bash + small node script) — saves you from complex server changes.
olivia: FYI we added REDWOOD_NO_RETRY flag in our infra image for flaky e2e flows; set it only where you need it.
alex_h: Thanks all — will update the PR and tag you @maria_s @samir for review.
